matches.quote: The model assumes a single isotropic 3D spherical Fermi surface ... linear-in-k basis functions ... include higher-harmonic basis functions.
Gap magnitudes are unphysically large... 2Δ/k_BT_c ≈ 13... This should be compared with existing UTe₂ STM and specific-heat gap estimates.
B₂u and B₃u are indistinguishable on the (001) surface... Measure on other facets ((100), (010) or (0−11)) to separate B₂u from B₃u
Normalization procedures, background subtraction and spreading-resistance corrections are not described.
At realistic Γ, the Aᵤ splitting (a feature smaller than Δ) is likely smeared into a single peak. Strongly anisotropic Aᵤ (as NMR suggests) is not explored.
the leap from spectral line shapes to an irreducible-representation (IR) assignment and a "single-parameter" phase discrimination rests on a minimal model
A transition between two different IRs ... implies either a first-order transition or an intermediate mixed (e.g., B₂u + iB₃u, TRS-breaking) state. Neither possibility is modelled.
The model assumes a single isotropic 3D spherical Fermi surface ... UTe₂ has quasi-2D cylindrical sheets along c ... could change the qualitative conclusions.
The critical-current test is applied only to the ambient-pressure ZBCP... It is never applied to the dips, which carry the central claim.
Test whether a fixed ratio with varying Γ and Z can reproduce the 0.6–0.8 GPa spectra; this is the critical null test.
The two-channel superposition model is introduced just where the single-channel fit fails, roughly doubling the free parameters without justification.
A transition between two different IRs within the superconducting state at a continuous phase line implies either a first-order transition or an intermediate mixed ... state.
The weighted ⟨Δ_z⟩/⟨Δ_x(y)⟩ then mixes physically distinct channels, so its continuity with the single-channel ratio at lower pressure is not meaningful.
At 1.4 GPa, close to MO1/MO2, the authors' own argument against magnetic (Kondo/Appelbaum-type) zero-bias anomalies no longer holds, yet this is not addressed.
All pressure data come from a single contact on a single sample (S1)... No pressure-release check is shown... No second pressurized contact or sample
No R_N values, contact-size estimate, or comparison with the elastic and inelastic mean free paths are given, so the ballistic/diffusive/thermal classification is unknown.
Table S1 and Fig. S7a label Δ_z and Δ_x(y) oppositely for the same fit. Read literally, Table S1 gives a ratio of about 1.8 at ambient pressure
No analysis disentangles Δ_z/Δ_x from Γ and Z. No parameter-correlation matrix, χ² landscape or confidence regions are provided.

notes: C12 is marked 'partly' because the review criticizes the restriction to linear-in-k basis functions and asks to include higher-harmonic basis functions (P6) and questions the exclusion of B1u (P22), without explicitly naming the k_x k_y k_z term. The review presents both 'Potential reasons for acceptance' and 'Potential reasons for rejection' along with actionable suggestions; 'major revision' (borderline 'reject' for a top-tier journal) is assigned.
